subject: Duration of Israelite sojourn and oppression in Egypt

figures.name: Years of sojourn/oppression
figures.note: All three textual traditions preserve the identical figure of 400 years, making this an exceptionally stable transmission.

systematic_analysis.pattern: Genesis 15:13 exhibits complete textual agreement across MT, LXX, and SP with the figure of 400 years. This stands in stark contrast to the divergences found in patriarchal chronologies (Genesis 5, 11) and represents one of the rare instances of unanimous numerical transmission. The round number (400) may have aided memorization and scribal fidelity, while its prophetic-covenant context may have discouraged alteration.
systematic_analysis.pattern_plain: All three ancient versions agree on 400 years, which is unusual since they often disagree on numbers. The round figure and its importance in God's covenant promise may have protected it from being changed.

theories.name: Universal Preservation
theories.summary: The unanimous 400-year figure reflects preservation from a common ancestral text predating the MT/LXX/SP divergence. The round number's mnemonic quality, its placement in divine speech, and its theological significance as a covenant prophecy created strong constraints against scribal modification. This represents the inverse of systematic divergence patterns seen elsewhere in Genesis.
theories.summary_plain: All three versions inherited the same number from an earlier shared source and no scribe felt free to change it because it was God's direct prophecy.
supporting_evidence: Textual unanimity across all major witnesses (MT, LXX, SP, and confirmed in ancient citations)
The figure appears in direct divine speech (Gen 15:13), elevating its sacred status and discouraging alteration
Round numbers (multiples of 100) demonstrate greater scribal stability across biblical transmission
Acts 7:6 and other Second Temple citations confirm the 400-year tradition was established early
Contrast with Genesis 5 and 11 chronologies where systematic divergences appear shows this stability is anomalous and therefore significant
weaknesses: Does not explain why this figure was preserved when other equally significant numbers (e.g., patriarchal ages) were not
The relationship to Exodus 12:40 (430 years) creates interpretive complexity that unanimous transmission does not resolve

theories.name: Theological Inviolability
theories.summary: The 400-year figure's preservation reflects theological constraints against modifying explicit divine prophecy. Unlike genealogical numbers which scribes felt latitude to adjust for chronological systems, direct quotes from God in covenant contexts were treated as sacrosanct. The figure's function as fulfilled prophecy (referenced in Acts 7:6, Josephus) reinforced its untouchable status across all textual traditions.
theories.summary_plain: Scribes were willing to change genealogies but not direct quotes from God, especially prophecies that had been famously fulfilled.
supporting_evidence: The number occurs within the Abrahamic covenant (Gen 15:7-21), the theological heart of the Pentateuch
Direct divine speech receives higher textual stability across biblical manuscripts than narrative or genealogical material
The prophecy's fulfillment status by Second Temple period created retrospective validation that discouraged alteration
Comparison with other covenant numbers (e.g., circumcision on 8th day) shows similar cross-textual stability
weaknesses: Other divine speeches contain numerical variants (e.g., flood chronology details), suggesting theological status alone is insufficient explanation
Does not account for why the related 430-year figure in Exodus 12:40 shows textual variation in LXX while this does not
Presumes scribes made conscious theological distinctions between types of numbers, which may be anachronistic

theories.name: Mnemonic Stability of Round Numbers
theories.summary: Round multiples of 100 demonstrate inherently greater resistance to corruption in textual transmission due to their mnemonic simplicity and ease of recognition. The 400-year figure's memorability reduced opportunity for inadvertent scribal error, while its roundness made intentional systematic adjustments (like the +100 year pattern in Genesis 11 LXX) mathematically awkward. This is primarily a preservation-through-simplicity argument rather than ideological.
theories.summary_plain: The number 400 is easy to remember and harder to accidentally copy wrong than complex numbers, so it stayed the same across all versions.
supporting_evidence: Round numbers show statistically lower variant rates across biblical manuscripts and versions
The figure's simplicity reduced transcription errors common with complex numbers in Hebrew/Greek numeral systems
Systematic chronological adjustments (+100 patterns) work cleanly with begetting ages but create awkwardness with round prophetic periods
weaknesses: Other round numbers in Scripture do show variation (e.g., 300 vs 360 in some textual traditions)
Cannot explain the theological selection of 400 rather than another round number
Mnemonic stability applies to oral transmission but manuscripts involved visual copying where round vs complex matters less

theories.name: Early Textual Fixation
theories.summary: The 400-year figure achieved textual fixation before the MT/LXX/SP traditions diverged, possibly as early as the Persian period or earlier. Unlike genealogical chronologies which remained fluid for chronographic purposes, this specific prophetic datum was already established in authoritative Temple texts or widely-memorized covenant recitations, preventing later divergence even as other numbers were adjusted in different textual families.
theories.summary_plain: This number was locked in place very early, before the different versions of the Bible split apart, while other numbers were still being adjusted.
supporting_evidence: The figure appears in pre-LXX citations and allusions suggesting established tradition by 3rd century BCE
Covenant formulations tend to stabilize earlier than genealogical materials in Ancient Near Eastern textual practice
The absence of any known variant reading across all witnesses (including Qumran fragments) suggests pre-divergence fixation
weaknesses: Difficult to prove timing of fixation without earlier manuscript evidence than currently available
Does not explain why this number fixated early while chronologically-adjacent numbers (Exodus 12:40) did not
Presumes a degree of textual authority in early periods that may not be warranted

overall_assessment: Genesis 15:13 represents a critical control case in patriarchal chronology studies: unanimous transmission across MT, LXX, and SP demonstrates that numerical divergence elsewhere is not random corruption but reflects systematic, tradition-specific tendencies. The 400-year figure's preservation likely results from converging factors: its status as direct divine speech in covenant context, its mnemonic simplicity as a round number, and probable early textual fixation before major textual families diverged. This stability inversely confirms that divergences in Genesis 5 and 11 stem from deliberate chronological recalculations rather than scribal carelessness. The contrast between this verse's unanimity and systematic inflation/deflation patterns elsewhere validates the methodological approach of scholars like Sexton and Green who identify ideological motivations behind chronological variants.
overall_plain: All ancient versions agree on 400 years, which is rare for numbers in Genesis. This agreement probably happened because it's God's direct prophecy, it's a round number easy to remember, and it was locked in early. The fact that this number stayed the same while others changed proves the other changes were deliberate, not accidents.

bibcrit_assessment.title: Unanimous Transmission Validates Systematic Divergence Theory
bibcrit_assessment.reasoning: The complete textual agreement on 400 years provides methodological validation for identifying systematic chronological adjustments elsewhere in Genesis. If numerical variants resulted from random scribal error, we would expect some divergence even here; instead, unanimity demonstrates scribes could preserve numbers faithfully when motivated. This inversely proves that divergences in Genesis 5 and 11 reflect intentional chronological programs (LXX inflation, MT deflation, SP harmonization) rather than transmission decay, fundamentally supporting the independent_traditions model with theological_motivation as the primary driver.
bibcrit_assessment.plain: Because all versions agree here, we know scribes could copy numbers accurately when they wanted to. This proves that when numbers differ elsewhere, it was on purpose, not by mistake.

_validation.confidence_note: Core claim of textual unanimity at Gen 15:13 is correct, but several supporting assertions are overstated, unverifiable, or potentially inaccurate.

flagged_claims.claim: Acts 7:6 and other Second Temple citations confirm the 400-year tradition was established early
flagged_claims.reason: Acts 7:6 is a New Testament text, not Second Temple Jewish literature in the technical sense; the framing conflates categories. Specific Second Temple citations are not named.

flagged_claims.claim: Round numbers show statistically lower variant rates across biblical manuscripts and versions
flagged_claims.reason: Presented as established statistical fact but no such systematic study is cited; this is a generalization that may not hold under scrutiny.

flagged_claims.claim: Other round numbers in Scripture do show variation (e.g., 300 vs 360 in some textual traditions)
flagged_claims.reason: Vague reference without specifying the passage; this specific 300/360 variant is not clearly identifiable and may be fabricated or misremembered.

flagged_claims.claim: The absence of any known variant reading across all witnesses (including Qumran fragments) suggests pre-divergence fixation
flagged_claims.reason: Implies Qumran preserves Gen 15:13; the verse's coverage in DSS (e.g., 4QGen fragments) should be verified before claiming absence of variants there.

flagged_claims.claim: validates the methodological approach of scholars like Sexton and Green
flagged_claims.reason: Jeremy Sexton has written on Genesis 5/11 chronology, but pairing with 'Green' (presumably W.H. Green) as joint methodological allies is imprecise; their positions differ significantly.

flagged_claims.claim: Comparison with other covenant numbers (e.g., circumcision on 8th day) shows similar cross-textual stability
flagged_claims.reason: Asserted without evidence; no demonstration that the 8th-day figure has been studied for cross-version stability.

flagged_claims.claim: the related 430-year figure in Exodus 12:40 shows textual variation in LXX while this does not
flagged_claims.reason: True that LXX/SP Ex 12:40 expand the formula (including sojourn in Canaan), but the claim is presented imprecisely—the number 430 itself is generally stable; the variation concerns the geographic scope.

safe_claims: MT, LXX, and SP all read 400 years at Gen 15:13
This stability contrasts with divergences in Genesis 5 and 11 chronologies
The figure occurs within direct divine speech in the Abrahamic covenant context (Gen 15:7-21)
